results.title: Power Electronics Reliability: State of the Art and Outlook
results.content: Index Terms—Accelerated degradation testing, condition monitoring, control, failure mechanism, physics-of-degradation, power electronics, reliability prediction. CONCLUSION This article reviews the latest power electronics reliability research in ﬁeld experiences, failure mechanisms, component-level EOL criteria, testing methods, and system-level mission-proﬁle-based reliability prediction methods. Finally, future research demands and opportunities are identiﬁed: 1) physics-of-degradation and condition monitoring; 2) accumulated damage modeling; 3) humidity-induced failure mechanisms, failure mechanisms of SiC MOSFETs, GaN devices, and magnetic components; 4) high-resolution and fast-temperature measurement; 5) reduction of reliability testing time; and 6) reliability modeling of power-electronics-based power systems. Blaabjerg, “Validation of lifetime prediction of IGBT modules based on linear damage accumulation by means of superimposed power cycling tests,” IEEE Trans. Ayyanar, “Accelerated testing of module-level power electronics for long-term reliability,” IEEE J. His research addresses the fundamental challenges in modeling and validation of power electronic component failure mechanisms and application issues in system-level predictability, condition monitoring, circuit architecture, and robustness design.
